subject: Behavioral Economics
title: Prospect Theory in Policy
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Prospect Theory in Policy.

hook.text: A carbon tax framed as 'climate action dividend' passes polls. The same tax framed as 'new tax' fails. Same policy.

buildup.text: Policymakers who understand framing design policies that feel like gains, not losses, for the public.

discovery.text: Prospect theory shapes voter behavior. Incumbents run on gains ('look what we achieved'). Challengers run on losses.

twist.text: Loss-framed policies often fail politically even when they're economically sound. Perception beats substance.

climax.text: Good policy isn't enough. It must be framed so citizens feel the gain, not the loss. Communication is policy.

punchline.text: Frame the policy right, or it won't get passed.

quiz.question: Why do some beneficial policies fail to gain public support?
options: The public understands all the details
They're framed as losses rather than gains
All policies eventually get public support
